questions.question: What is the default trigger for a `@defer` block when none is specified?
questions.explanation: Without an explicit trigger, `@defer` uses `on idle`, loading the deferred chunk once the browser is idle (via requestIdleCallback).

questions.question: What does `@defer (on interaction; prefetch on hover)` do?
options: Downloads the chunk when the user hovers, and renders the content when they click or press a key
Renders the content on hover and removes it on click
Downloads and renders the content on hover; the interaction trigger is ignored
Prefetches the chunk at build time and renders it on hover
questions.explanation: `prefetch` only downloads the chunk. The main trigger (`on interaction`) decides when the content is actually rendered, so the code is usually ready by the time the user clicks.

questions.question: You wrapped a chart component in `@defer`, but the main bundle did not get smaller. What is the most likely cause?
options: `@defer` blocks are always bundled eagerly in production builds
You forgot to add an `@error` block
The same component is also referenced outside the `@defer` block (in the template or class), so it must stay in the main bundle
questions.explanation: Only standalone dependencies used exclusively inside the `@defer` block are split into the lazy chunk. Any other reference in the same component keeps them eager.

questions.question: Which router configuration preloads every lazy route in the background after the app bootstraps?
questions.explanation: `withPreloading(PreloadAllModules)` fetches all lazy chunks once the app is idle. `NoPreloading` is the default, and a custom PreloadingStrategy can preload selectively.
